text.p: Privately held Arron Ltd of Hong Kong has transferred free of charge six million legal person shares of textile maker Shanghai Haixin Co to another private firm, Haixin said in a statement published in the Shanghai Securities on Thursday.
The shares, representing 3.54 percent of Shanghai-listed Haixin, were transferred to Rich Development Co as part of a divorce settlement by Arron chairman Ke Qingsheng.
Arron had owned 22 million shares or 12.99 percent of Haixin's total of 169.4 million shares before the transfer, the newspaper said.

Legal person shares were designed as a special class of equity aimed at state institutional shareholders to maintain government control over state corporations that offer some of their shares to the public.
But many of these state institutional shares have ended up in private hands, undermining the intent of the creation of this type of stock.
Some brokers have argued that companies should be able to sell legal person shares without any restrictions and make them available to the public.
Haixin's B shares for foreign investors were suspended in morning trade. They closed at $0.556 on Wednesday.
